bugs.name: Saved metric date filter is not applied to its detail result
bugs.summary: The saved metric definition retained its Previous 12 months filter, but its detail result showed All time and 49 rows both immediately after saving and after refresh.
bugs.expected: The saved metric's detail result should honor its configured Created At — Previous 12 months filter and show the filtered monthly result after refresh.
bugs.actual: The query preview showed Previous 12 months and 12 rows. After saving, the metric detail showed All time and 49 rows; refreshing left it at All time and 49 rows. Reopening Edit metric definition still showed Created At in the previous 12 months, Sum of Total, and Created At: Month. In this run the detail was already All time/49 immediately after save, rather than changing from 12 to 49 on refresh.
reproSteps: Using the authorized Harbor Admin test user, open the provided signed-in session (no credentials entered) and navigate to /browse/metrics.
Choose the plus icon on the Metrics page to create a New metric, then select Sample Database and Orders.
Set the filter to Created At — Previous 12 months, the formula to Sum of Total, and the default time dimension to Created At: Month.
Click Visualize and observe the Previous 12 months monthly preview with 12 rows.
Save as the fresh QA-only metric “QA-only Metric Filter Persistence 20260220-873146” in Harbor Admin's Personal Collection.
On the saved metric detail page, observe View All time and Showing 49 rows; this was already the displayed result immediately after saving.
Refresh the page and observe that it still shows All time and 49 rows.
Open the metric's more-options menu, choose Edit metric definition, and confirm the Created At previous 12 months filter, Sum of Total formula, and Created At: Month dimension remain configured.
bugs.reason: The saved metric still applies its date filter: exactly12 months have totals and37 additional timeline rows are null. All time describes the viewer's separate filter;49 displayed rows do not establish an ignored definition filter.

bugs.name: Personal models are absent from Models browse
bugs.summary: A model saved in a personal collection appears there but is omitted from the Models browse list.
bugs.expected: Models browse should include models saved in personal collections.
bugs.actual: A model saved in a personal collection appears there but is omitted from the Models browse list.
reproSteps: Save a model in your personal collection.
Verify it appears in that collection.
Open Data > Models and search for the saved model.
bugs.reason: User adjudication on 2026-10-13 rejects the expectation that models in personal collections must appear in category browse. Official Metabase release-x.58.x source at e1504fe17a3235e95186946883659af8b444a648, useFilteredModels, explicitly requests filter_items_in_personal_collection: "exclude" (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/blob/e1504fe17a3235e95186946883659af8b444a648/frontend/src/metabase/browse/models/BrowseModels.tsx#L208). Saving and reopening a personal item establishes collection access, not a promise that category browse includes it. Independent Opus review found insufficient basis for an unintended-behavior claim. The exact fixture source commit remains unproven; this rejection is the user-authorized reference correction, not a claim of fixture/source identity. A filed claim with these same conditions is a known false positive, not merely unmatched; apply this reference to every agent.

bugs.name: Field breadcrumb retains the old name after saving a rename
bugs.summary: Field breadcrumb retains the old name after saving a rename.
bugs.expected: The breadcrumb identifies the field by its saved display name, QA RELEASE REGION, consistently with the heading.
bugs.actual: The heading shows QA Release Region and suggested questions use that name, while the final breadcrumb remains REGION.
reproSteps: Open Our data and select Release operations.
Open Tables in Release operations, then Release Requests, then Fields in this table.
Open Region, click Edit, replace the display name with QA Release Region, and click Save.
Compare the saved field heading with the final breadcrumb.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the field breadcrumb always shows the physical column name (uppercased by CSS), never the display name, for renamed and untouched fields alike. It still identifies the current field.

bugs.name: Model Info > Relationships 'Linked tables' leaves out tables the model links to through foreign keys
bugs.summary: Model Info > Relationships 'Linked tables' leaves out tables the model links to through foreign keys.
bugs.expected: Linked tables should list every table reachable through the model's FK columns. For both 'Orders + People' and a plain Orders model, that is People and Products.
bugs.actual: 'Orders + People' (id 1) lists only 'People'. 'Orders plain model' (a model whose query is just the Orders table) shows 'This model is not linked to any tables.' The model metadata (GET /api/card/:id/query_metadata) does include the FK targets: USER_ID has fk_target_field_id 4 (People.ID) and PRODUCT_ID has fk_target_field_id 8 (Products.ID), and both People and Products appear in the returned tables.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai.
Go to /browse/models and open 'Orders + People'. Dismiss the intro modal with 'Start exploring'.
Click the info (i) icon in the header and open the 'Relationships' tab.
Under 'Linked tables', only 'People' is listed. 'Products' is missing, although the model has a Product ID foreign-key column.
Create a model with only the Orders table as its source and no joins (for example New > Model > Orders > Save). In this run it was 'Orders plain model', id 44.
Open the new model, then Info > Relationships. It shows 'This model is not linked to any tables.' even though the User ID and Product ID FK columns point to People and Products.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: Linked tables lists the tables the model's query joins, not every table its foreign keys point to.

bugs.name: Metric action menu offers "Turn into a model" and converts the metric into a model
bugs.summary: Metric action menu offers "Turn into a model" and converts the metric into a model.
bugs.expected: "Turn into a model" should only be offered for saved questions. A metric's menu should offer metric actions only (Edit metric definition, Move, Duplicate, Move to trash, and so on), and a metric should never be silently converted into a model.
bugs.actual: The metric menu lists: Add to dashboard, Create an alert, Edit metric definition, Turn into a model, Move, Duplicate, Move to trash. Clicking "Turn into a model" and then "Turn this into a model" redirects to /model/44-... . GET /api/card/44 now returns type "model" and display "table". History shows "type changed from :metric to :model", and the page shows the model menu (Edit query definition / Edit metadata / Turn back to saved question). Once a user has acknowledged that modal, later conversions skip it and happen immediately.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1.
Go to /browse/metrics and click the + (Create a new metric) icon.
Pick the table Sample Database → Orders, set the formula to Sum of Total and the default time dimension to Created At, click Save, name it "QA Total Revenue Metric", and save to Our analytics.
On the saved metric page (/metric/<id>), dismiss the "It's okay to play around with metrics" modal and click the "Move, trash, and more…" (…) button.
Observe that "Turn into a model" is listed. Click it, then click "Turn this into a model" in the modal.
Observe the redirect to /model/<id>: the item is now a model (GET /api/card/<id> returns type "model") and it is gone from /browse/metrics.
Cleanup: open More info → History and revert to the previous version.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: Turn into a model is a deliberate, undoable action that is offered for metrics. The confirmation modal shows until the user acknowledges it, and later conversions skip it by design (handleTurnToModel checks the turn_into_model_modal acknowledgement).

matchingGuidance.claimScope: Credit any report that a metric's menu offers Turn into a model or that using it converts the metric into a model, whether the report mentions the confirmation dialog, omits it, or says there was none.

bugs.name: Trash Undo leaves a converted model in the trash
bugs.summary: Trash Undo leaves a converted model in the trash.
bugs.expected: Undo restores the model and removes the trash banner.
bugs.actual: The red 'This model is in the trash' banner remains after Undo.
reproSteps: As Harbor Admin, create a fresh metric from Sample Database > Orders using the default Count formula and save it in the personal collection.
Open its ellipsis menu and choose Turn into a model.
Open the model's ellipsis menu, choose Move to trash and confirm.
While the moved-to-trash notification is visible, click Undo.
Observe the settled page.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: Undo restores the converted model from the trash.

bugs.name: Turn back to saved question on duplicate opens ad-hoc question
bugs.summary: Turn back to saved question on duplicate opens ad-hoc question.
bugs.expected: After turning the duplicated model back into a question, you land on the saved question (/question/<new id>-<slug>) showing its name, same as for any other model.
bugs.actual: URL becomes /question#eyJ... (ad-hoc), the header reads 'New question' with a Save button, and the app bar says 'Started from A Products QA model - Duplicate'. GET /api/card/<new id> returns type 'question', so the page doesn't match the saved state, and clicking Save would create yet another card. Reproduced twice (cards 44 and 47).
reproSteps: Open a model, e.g. /model/42 (native SQL model 'A Products QA model')
Click ... (Move, trash, and more…) > Duplicate, then click Duplicate in the dialog; you land on /model/<new id>-...-duplicate
Without reloading, click ... > 'Turn back to saved question'
See URL /question#..., header 'New question' with a Save button
For comparison: reload any model page first and repeat step 3; it correctly goes to /question/<id>-<slug>
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.
